name: Genetic Biliary Tract Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Genetic Biliary Tract Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic mutation in genes associated with biliary tract disease
Biochemical evidence of cholestasis including elevated alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase
Imaging evidence of biliary tract abnormalities such as bile duct dilatation or strictures on MRCP or ERCP
Positive family history of biliary tract disease or related liver disorders
Liver biopsy showing bile duct paucity, fibrosis, or ductular reaction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic genetic mutation plus biochemical and imaging evidence of biliary tract disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of acquired causes of biliary tract disease.

laboratory: Elevated alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase
imaging: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) showing bile duct irregularities
Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) demonstrating strictures or dilatations
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as ABCB4, JAG1, or NOTCH2 depending on subtype
other: Liver biopsy showing bile duct paucity, fibrosis, or ductular proliferation

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of known pathogenic genetic mutations
Rapid progression to liver failure without surgical intervention

redFlags: Rapidly progressive cholestasis in infancy or childhood
Signs of portal hypertension or liver failure
